description: rg -rn is never a valid flag combo: rg parses -r <text> as REPLACE-with-literal. Run 01M22X87J1RKQ6A8FZB7RC2RN8: 'rg -rn "is_engine_stamped_key"' replaced every match with literal 'n', producing 'pub fn n(key: &str...)', which was then misdiagnosed as 'sandbox rg unreliable' (false lore, cost 2 diagnostic rounds). Use -n alone for line numbers.
resolution: Discipline line added to .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md retracting the 'sandbox rg unreliable' lore (seed fabro-2eb6).

content: fabro-api-client regen without a working java: run the SAME pinned generator via Docker (openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:v7.20.0 generate -i <spec> -o /local/lib/packages/fabro-api-client/src with the repo mounted at /local), then bun run scripts/normalize-generated.ts, then fix root-owned output via an alpine chown sidecar (bun re-creates files through directory write access). LOCAL test-stack deploys are ALWAYS just up (cached loop: SPA, binary, image, CLI, compose) — docker compose up --build builds nothing here and cargo build -p <name> drifts with upstream package renames; PRODUCTION is just image-release + fabro-tofu apply, never hand-composed.

description: Changing the embedded FABRO_GIT_SHA length (fabro_build_support::SHORT_SHA_LEN, fabro-6ffb 7->12) silently breaks the fabro-test insta BUILD filter regex (lib/foundation/fabro-test/src/lib.rs INSTA_FILTERS, the ([0-9a-f]{7} date...) pattern) because the filter hardcodes the old length: version snapshots then diff on every commit. Length-bearing snapshot filters must be updated in the same diff as the length constant; symptom is a snapshot diff showing a raw sha where [BUILD] used to be.
resolution: Updated the filter to {12} in the same diff (fabro-6ffb); future length changes must grep INSTA_FILTERS for the old length before landing.

description: Piping  into a python one-liner that crashes still creates the record — the CLI already wrote it (fabro sprint 19: d7e7+3523 silently duplicated f93b+c167 and had to be closed as dupes). Same class as the fabro create ghost-run rule.
resolution: write seeds CLI json to a FILE first, then parse the file; never pipe create-family commands into a consumer that can die; sweep the tracker diff for surprise new ids before committing

description: Run-stage scripts invoking mise-wrapped commands (just qualitygate, sd) fail with 'Config files in /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml are not trusted' whenever the sandbox/home is recycled or .mise.toml changes, killing the whole stage before any code runs (run 01M1XCHJTDBJKZ31VFMY1KD61Q tester stage).
resolution: Immediate: 'mise trust /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml' once per environment (done this session). Durable: stage bootstrap or justfile entry should export MISE_YES=1 or pre-trust before invoking mise-dependent recipes.

description: Semantics change in fabro-tool inherit_parent_target (fabro-b4ed, run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC) passed the implementer's crate-scoped verify but red-lined the tester: the fabro-server integration fixture lib/apps/fabro-server/src/run_tool_create.rs builds a parent via test_run_spec() whose pull_request settings stay None, so under the new option-(a) semantics the child correctly inherits the base branch and the checkout assertion reads 'original'. Lesson: any change to inherited-target semantics must update downstream fixture parents to enable pull_request settings when the test means to exercise run-branch chaining. Also: after editing a src-integrated test file, confirm nextest actually recompiled — a stale binary reported the pre-edit panic line.
resolution: Fixture parent now sets pull_request enabled before inherit, matching the new chaining precondition; test passes and full fabro-server suite is green (939/939).

description: A tracker close reason containing BACKTICKS was passed through the bash() command line (seeds close <id> --reason "..."): bash executed the backticked fragments as command substitution. 'start -> env_guard -> tracker_guard' ran the command 'start' with stdout REDIRECTED to env_guard and tracker_guard, which CREATED three empty files at the repo root; the recorded close reason lost every backticked phrase. It went unnoticed until but status showed three 'A' entries beside the tracker file.
resolution: For any CLI write whose text may contain backticks, $() or >, write the payload to a file and pass it as --reason "$(cat /tmp/reason.txt)" (command substitution happens once, on that path only). After every shell-based tracker write, run but status / git status and remove stray A entries before committing — a stray file would otherwise ride the next sweep commit.
